title: outlineR: Artefact Processing and Extraction Protocol
author: David Nicolas Matzig
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bygaptse
materials: under Files of type select JPEG Bitmap,

steps.title: Set Up Project Directory Structure
steps.instruction: Create a project folder named "/project_folder" with a specific subfolder hierarchy to organize raw and processed data.

substeps.instruction: Create /project_folder/raw for raw image data.
Create /project_folder/prep for prepared image data.
Create /project_folder/prep/single for single artefacts.
Create /project_folder/data/raw_data for external data.
Create /project_folder/data/derived_data for generated analysis data.

steps.title: Prepare Raw Images
steps.instruction: Save the source image (e.g., Morar Quartz Industry from Wellcome Collection) into "/project_folder/raw" as "morar_quartz_industry.jpg". Ensure files are in .jpg format with no special characters or spaces in the filenames.

steps.title: Manually Clean Images in GIMP
steps.instruction: Use GIMP (version 2.8 on Ubuntu 18.04) to isolate the artefacts from the background and non-artefact elements.

substeps.instruction: Load the raw image from /project_folder/raw/.
Remove numbering, scales, text, ventral/lateral views, and incomplete artefacts using the Rectangle select tool and the delete key.
Convert the image to grayscale via Image → Mode → Grayscale.
Binarize the image via Color → Threshold to create thick lines around artefacts.
Remove any stray pixels created during thresholding.
Close any gaps in the artefact outlines using the Pencil tool (Hardness 100, Pixel Size 1).
Save the prepared image in /project_folder/prep using the original filename at 100% detail, without changing size, scaling, or DPI.

steps.title: Create TPS File using tpsUtil32
steps.instruction: Generate a .tps file containing the filenames of the prepared images using tpsUtil32 (v1.81, Windows).

substeps.instruction: Navigate to Operations → Build tps file from images.
In the Input directory field, navigate to /project_folder/raw, select a picture, set Files of type to JPEG Bitmap, and click Open.
In the Output file field, navigate to /project_folder/raw and create a .tps file using underscores instead of spaces and no special characters.
In the Actions field, click Setup, ensure 'Include all' is checked, 'do not include path' is selected, and click Create.

steps.title: Determine Scaling Factor in tpsDig
steps.instruction: Use tpsDIG2w32 (v2.31, Windows) to derive the pixel-to-centimeter scaling factor based on the raw image scale bars.

substeps.instruction: Load the .tps file via File → Input source → File.
In the Image Tools window (Options → Image tools...):
1. Set scale.
2. Click the starting and end points of the scale in the image.
3. Enter the length of the reference scale.
4. Verify the unit of measure (e.g., cm, mm).
5. Click OK.
6. Use the red right-arrow in the top left corner to proceed to the next image if applicable.

steps.title: Initialize R Environment
steps.instruction: Set up the R environment (R ≥ 3.6.3) and RStudio (≥ 1.2.5033) for outline extraction.

substeps.instruction: Install the outlineR package using: remotes::install_github("yesdavid/outlineR", dependencies = TRUE).
Create a new RStudio project: File → New Project... → Existing Directory → navigate to /project_folder → Create Project.
Open a new R script: File → New File → R Script.

steps.title: Extract Single Artefacts via outlineR
steps.instruction: Use the outlineR package to separate individual artefacts from the prepared images.

substeps.instruction: Load the library: library(outlineR).
Define the input path (inpath <- file.path(".", "prep")) and output path (outpath <- file.path(".", "prep", "single")).
Execute the extraction: outlineR::separate_single_artefacts(inpath = inpath, outpath = outpath).

Verify that images are saved in /prep/single with names ending in "_pseudo_no_" followed by a number. If empty images appear, check for stray pixels or open outlines in the prepared images and re-run.

steps.title: Extract and Combine Outlines
steps.instruction: Convert the .tps file to a data frame and extract the scaled outlines of the separated artefacts.

substeps.instruction: Import the .tps file: tps_df <- outlineR::tps_to_df("path/to/tps/file.tps").
Extract outlines and apply scaling: single_outlines_list <- outlineR::get_outlines(outpath = outpath, tps_file_rescale = tps_df). (If no .tps file exists, set tps_file_rescale = NULL).
Combine outlines into a Momocs 'Out' file: outlines_combined <- outlineR::combine_outlines(single_outlines_list = single_outlines_list).

steps.title: Validate Extracted Outlines
steps.instruction: Inspect the combined outlines for errors and validity using Momocs and base R functions.

substeps.instruction: Check the number of outlines: length(outlines_combined).
Visualize stacked outlines: stack(outlines_combined).
Visualize all outlines side-by-side: Momocs::panel(outlines_combined).
Inspect outlines individually: Momocs::inspect(outlines_combined).
